results.claim: Swish containment is exactly a multiplicity-respecting directed-cycle problem.
results.proof_sketch: Let G={1,H,V,R} act on the 12 grid positions. Represent a card (p,q), after transformation g, by the arc gp→gq. In a swish, every occupied position has indegree and outdegree one, so its arcs are a disjoint union of directed simple cycles. Conversely, the cards forming any directed simple cycle constitute a swish. Thus a card collection is no-swish exactly when no directed simple cycle can be formed using each physical card at most once.

results.claim: A no-swish collection contains at most 20 distinct transformation types, and this is sharp.
results.proof_sketch: The position orbits under G are A={(1,1),(1,3),(4,1),(4,3)}, B={(1,2),(4,2)}, C={(2,1),(2,3),(3,1),(3,3)}, and D={(2,2),(3,2)}, of sizes 4,2,4,2. There are eight card types whose two endpoints lie in the same position-orbit: three each on A,C and one each on B,D. The remaining 28 types form 14 pairs {t,t*}, where t* reverses hoop and ball. Using both t and t* makes a 2-card swish, so at most 14 cross-orbit types occur. On either four-point orbit, the three internal types correspond to the three nonidentity elements of the Klein group and together form a directed triangle; hence at most two occur. The two-point orbits contribute at most one type each. Therefore the support has size at most 14+2+2+1+1=20. Sharpness follows by ordering A,B,C,D, taking all 14 cross-orbit types directed forward in this order, two internal types on each of A,C, and the sole internal type on each of B,D. Cross arcs strictly increase the orbit order, while the chosen internal cards contain no cycle.

results.claim: Unless all eight internal types are duplicated, the usual once-or-twice interpretation of the 60-card deck already yields a 29-card no-swish subset.
results.proof_sketch: Assume the 36 transformation types all occur and every multiplicity is one or two. Let M0 be the number of physical cards belonging to the eight internal types. Choose the six-card internal no-swish set used above. For any total order of A,B,C,D, add every cross-orbit physical card directed forward in that order. The result is no-swish because a cycle cannot contain a strictly order-increasing arc. Averaged over the 24 orders, each cross-orbit card is selected with probability 1/2. Hence some order gives at least 6+ceil((60−M0)/2) cards. If any internal type is not duplicated, then M0≤15 and this bound is at least 29. Consequently only the case M0=16—all eight internal types duplicated—can possibly have maximum 28.

results.claim: The authorized input omits information essential to deciding the exact commercial-deck target.
results.proof_sketch: Two abstract 60-card decks satisfy all stated type-count information but have opposite answers. Start with one copy of every one of the 36 types. For Deck X, double all eight internal types and both members of any eight of the 14 reversal pairs. It has 60 cards. Any no-swish subset has at most six internal cards, at most two cards from each doubled reversal pair, and at most one from each remaining pair, totaling 6+8·2+6=28; the forward-order construction attains 28. For Deck Y, fix an order of A,B,C,D, double nine of the 14 forward cross-types, and double any other 15 types. Selecting both copies of those nine types, one copy of each remaining forward cross-type, and the six safe internal cards gives 18+5+6=29 no-swish cards. Thus the identities of the duplicated commercial types—not supplied in source_paper_text—are indispensable.

final_writeup:
The problem reduces cleanly to a finite directed-cycle problem, and the only unresolved information is deck-specific.

There are exactly 36 geometric card types: Burnside’s lemma gives (132+12)/4=36, since horizontal reflection fixes the 12 ordered pairs of distinct middle-column positions, while vertical reflection and 180-degree rotation fix none. Six types have transformation orbits of size two and 30 have size four.

Every no-swish collection uses at most 20 distinct types. More importantly, under the source’s apparent once-or-twice multiplicity convention, a 29-card no-swish subset necessarily exists unless all eight types whose endpoints lie in one position-orbit are duplicated. In that remaining case the exact identities of the 16 duplicated cross-orbit types matter.

Those identities are not enumerated in the authorized JSON. They cannot be inferred merely from “60 cards” and “36 distinct cards up to symmetry”: the two explicit abstract multiplicity patterns in Claim 4 satisfy those data but have respective maxima 28 and at least 29. Therefore I cannot rigorously claim FULL resolution for the original physical deck from the permitted input alone. A complete certificate now requires only the 36-entry multiplicity vector of the commercial deck; the cycle formulation above then gives a direct finite verification problem.
checks_performed: Read only the specified JSON input; no web or other repository files were consulted.
Enumerated the 132 ordered pairs on the 4×3 grid under the four allowed transformations, obtaining 36 types: 30 orbits of size four and six of size two.

Generated every transformed arc of every type and used an integer-state depth-first search over directed simple cycles of lengths 2 through 12 to check the sharp 20-type construction and the conditional 29-card construction.
Independently checked the 20-type upper bound by partitioning the 36 types into 14 reverse pairs, two internal triples, and two internal singletons.
